name: Lux Foods
long_description: Lux Foods engineers ultra-compact plants that produce mostly fruit, then grows them on sugar with 90% less light. We design the biology and hardware together to make robotic farming easier. Starting with cherry tomatoes, we’re building year-round production of flavorful, nutritious, pesticide-free fruit near the people who eat it. Our tomatoes have been grown on the International Space Station, and now we're taking this technology to Earth.
one_liner: Crops engineered for premium fruit, grown without sunlight.

founders.title: Founder/CEO
founders.founder_bio: CEO & co-founder at Lux Foods. Stanford BioE/Computer Science (AI) B.S./B.S.. First lab student in Dr. Robert Jinkerson's lab at UC Riverside, leading project on endosymbiotic gene transfer in algae. Previously student researcher at Brophy Lab working on synthetic genetic circuits in plants. Founded Fruit for Homeless nonprofit, leading 25 students to rescue and distribute 300,000 pounds of fresh fruit to underserved LA communities. Regeneron STS Semi-finalist, iGEM silver medalist.

founders.title: Founder
founders.founder_bio: Co-founder & CSO at Lux Foods. Professor of Chemical Engineering at UC Riverside since 2017, engineering crops for controlled environments and space. Led the UCR team that won NASA's Deep Space Food Challenge and flew cherry tomatoes to the ISS. NSF CAREER Award, FFAR New Innovator Award. Showed plants can grow on acetate without sunlight (Nature Food 2022). Previously postdoc at Stanford; PhD, Colorado School of Mines.

launches.title: Lux Foods: Crops engineered for premium fruit, grown without sunlight.
launches.body:
**tl;dr: Premium fruit, engineered for abundance.**

Lux Foods is redesigning plant biology and hardware together to build a future of food that is affordable, abundant, and exceptional.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y6T7PEmW9Wg>

**About Lux Foods**

For generations, the seasons, weather, and geography have determined what we grow and where. We built a global supply chain to move the harvest to the customer.

We want to bring the harvest closer.

At Lux, we engineer compact plants around the fruit we actually eat. Plants normally use light to make sugars through photosynthesis with \~1% conversion efficiency. We supply these sugars and nutrients directly through a growing medium, allowing them to grow under 90% lower light intensity. By supplying carbon externally, we reduce the fruiting plant’s dependence on fixing that carbon itself and gain more freedom to design both the crop and its growing environment. Starting from small pieces of cultured plant tissue, we regenerate small plantlets that develop mostly flowers and fruit. Agricultural robots historically contend with hidden fruit, variable plant architecture, and deformable tissue. We’re constraining the task distribution through simplified plant biology and hardware designed together, making farming easier for robots to learn.

Starting with tomatoes, we’re building toward year-round, pesticide-free production near our customers. Shorter journeys give us more freedom to choose varieties for flavor and nutrition, rather than their ability to survive shipping. For chefs and grocers, that means a dependable supply of distinctive varieties; for their customers, better-tasting fruit in every season.

**Built for space. Grown for Earth.**

Lux's biology was born in the Jinkerson Lab at UC Riverside, where the big question was how to grow fresh food in the most constrained environment imaginable: a spacecraft. With support from NASA and the Gates Foundation, the lab developed gene-edited tomato plants that put nearly all of their growth into fruit, with almost no stem or leaves, and grow with far less light than a conventional plant. Those tomatoes flew to the International Space Station in 2025. The same traits that make a plant viable in orbit, small footprint, low light, minimal waste biomass, are exactly what make dense, automated production possible on Earth.

**What if the grocery market was the farm?**

Our ambition is to bring growing, harvesting, and packing under one roof, and ultimately closer to where food is sold, cooked, and eaten. A repeatable production system could make exceptional crop varieties practical far beyond the regions and seasons where they thrive today. Heirloom, rare, and wild fruit could become everyday food. We’re building our first farm in San Francisco, and tomatoes are the starting point. The goal is a broad portfolio of excellent whole foods, produced reliably and at scale.

**The Lux Team**

We’re Andre Yeung and Robert Jinkerson.

Andre (CEO) trained in Bioengineering and Computer Science at Stanford, because he believes the next generation of food is inevitable and comes from the synthesis of living systems and useful machines. Previously, he researched plant synthetic genetic circuits and founded a nonprofit that rescued and distributed 300,000 lbs of fresh fruit to low-income communities in Los Angeles. Robert (CSO) is an associate professor of chemical and environmental engineering at UC Riverside and has spent 18 years engineering photosynthetic organisms for food, fuels, and materials because he believes biology is the most powerful manufacturing platform we have. Andre joined Robert’s lab in 2017 and their plant biotechnology research underpins Lux’s approach to low-light production. Together, we’re turning that science into a new way to make and serve exceptional food.

The next harvest grows where you live.

Lux Foods. Fruit, by design.

**If you’re a chef, produce distributor, foodservice operator, or grocery buyer, we’d love to hear what you want to source and explore a pilot or future supply relationship. Learn more and book a meeting at [luxfoods.xyz](http://luxfoods.xyz).**
